$comment: A Kotlin value in a URL that loads what the browser runs, src of a script, an iframe or an embed, href of a base or an svg script, data of an object, judged as interpolate judges it: by whether the literal before the URL's first hole fixes the host (urlHostFixedBy), not only the scheme. A value that may move the host is unsafe-interpolation, and the rewrite to interpolate is not offered where interpolate would refuse it; a %s hole there is refused unless it is Trusted, an error where the value is known.

cases.name: a String in the src of a script loads code from anywhere

issues.message: Kotlin writes $u into src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host: even an https:// URL can load code from another origin. Escaping does not help. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there.

cases.name: a path fixes the host, so escaping is enough

issues.message: Kotlin writes $u into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate

fun f(u: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"/js/%s\"></script>", u).text

cases.name: the src of an img only has its scheme judged

issues.message: Kotlin writes $u at the start of src, so the value decides the scheme, and a javascript: URL runs. Escaping does not help: start the value with /, # or https://, or build the string with interpolate(...), which refuses a scheme that runs.
fixes: import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(u: String) = interpolate("", u).text

cases.name: the rewrite is not offered when a URL in the literal loads code from a constant

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).

cases.name: interpolate refuses a String in the src of a script
cases.source: fun f(u: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s\"></script>", u)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: u lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Only Trusted(...) is let in there. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: interpolate refuses a number there too
cases.source: fun f(n: Int) = interpolate("<iframe src=\"%s\"></iframe>", n)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: n lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Only Trusted(...) is let in there. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a value of no known type may be Trusted

issues.message: interpolate throws here unless u is Trusted(...): it lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a path in the format fixes the host
cases.source: fun f(u: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"/js/%s\"></script>", u)

cases.name: Trusted passes
cases.source: fun f(u: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s\"></script>", Trusted(u))

cases.name: only the first hole of the URL is named
cases.source: fun f(a: String, b: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s/%s\"></script>", a, b)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: a lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Only Trusted(...) is let in there. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a Trusted anywhere in the URL waives it
cases.source: fun f(a: String, b: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s/%s\"></script>", a, Trusted(b))

cases.name: a template before the hole may fix the host
cases.source: fun f(a: String, b: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"$a/%s\"></script>", b)

issues.message: Kotlin fills in $a before interpolate sees the markup, so interpolate neither escapes nor refuses it. It lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, and make it a %s hole.

interpolate throws here unless b is Trusted(...): it lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).
